svg.title: TOPAK drawn as a railway line diagram
svg.desc: Ten coloured lines and forty-seven stations. The consensus log is drawn as a river: lines decide on its north bank and take effect on its south bank. Every station is listed in the index below the map.

g.title: THINKER SEAT (A3). A Persona in a confined guest, Byzantine by premise. It speaks one typed alphabet: six variants in Build, three in Run.
LAUNCHER (B3). Starts a guest from a promoted profile, appraises it, grants, and bridges its channel.
VERIFIER ‡ (B3). An independent verifier appraises rung-3 evidence under an issued key and returns a signed verdict.
FRONT DOOR (B3). Exposes the alphabet and nothing else.
EPOCH FENCE (B3). Local expiry, then the epoch fence. An action under a fenced epoch is rejected by the mechanism, not by policy.
LEASE (C3). The one composite credential, twelve fields. It ends with its round, renewal only narrows it, and revoking it needs no quorum.
LIFT (C3). Syntactic lift to one frozen input. Semantic judgment is never a lift.

POLICY FLOOR * (D3). Permits only what the floor allows, over schema S, and any error is a deny. It decides control requests alone, and entry R3 refuses a Thinker's effect without a live cell Observer.
BUNDLE (D3). A signed bundle, evaluated at the lease's revision. It can refuse and can never grant: admit ⟺ floor_permit ∧ ¬bundle_deny.
DENIED (E3). A denial is recorded, unordered, with digests only. It never crosses the log.
APPLY (F3). At its log position every entry is checked again: fence, lease, alphabet. If one has moved the admit is void: ordered, recorded, no effect.
EFFECT (F3). The effect executor performs an effect only after its admit commits.
TOOL HOST (G3). Gives a tool its workspace or its one declared channel, and nothing else. Handles are resolved on the mechanism's side.
THE WORLD (H3). The tools' targets: what Run acts on. Reached only by Actuate, on the allowlist entry's declared channel.
WORKSPACE (G3). Build's round-scoped workspace, where Draft writes.
SUBMIT & SEAL (G3). Submit(digest) seals the workspace and the topic set. It is Build's sole egress.
INTENT (E1). The sole axiom. Everything below it is issued, voted or derived.
ANCHOR † (E1). A havoc issuer. Its key-holders sign the rules and stand at the gate, outside the proofs.
RULES FLOOR (F1). Bounds every anchor issuance, R1 to R9 (R8 withdrawn). An issuance outside it is rejected.
RULES (F1). Rosters, seat declarations, quorum, keys and the two lists the load checks read. Genesis rules are resident.
GRANT SEATS (G1). Human voters, Mediated. Each vote is bound to the artifact, the evidence and the rules epoch, and the author is recused.
PROMOTION TALLY § (G2). Promotion is a unanimous quorum grant, counted at apply: Promoted, Pending, Stalled or Denied. A timeout never grants.
GATES § (G2). Totality, non-vacuity, discrimination. Each vote covers the evidence digest.
SIGN § (F2). The bundle key signs after the tally and never before.
ROLL OUT † (C3). A promoted revision reaches a live principal when its round ends: the next lease names it. A promotion seats.

WORKFLOW ENGINE (F1). Loads a workflow only from a promoted artifact, grants each slot under the promotion's authority, evaluates guards over settled attributes, and checks a route at decide and again at apply.
ORCHESTRATOR (D1). Chooses one enabled edge with Route(edge). It is given handles, never bytes. It can stall a workflow and cannot misroute it.
IDENTITY PROVIDER ‡ (A5). Vouches for the person behind an operator's key: a sign-on assertion naming the key and a fence.
OPERATOR SEAT (B5). A person and a principal. One operator keeps a quorum's grant going and may only narrow it.
CONTROL (C5). Six signed actions. Three add: Regrant, Renew, AttestGates. Three deny: EndRound, Revoke, FenceEpoch. Floor entries C1 to C9 decide them with no bundle, and a deny needs no lease.
ROSTER (A4). The break-glass roster. Its quorum signs an activation.
ACTIVATION (B4). One person, one seating, one round, with the task. The Activate entry is forensic class F5.
EMERGENCY SEAT (B4). One lease, no successor and no renewal, on an ordinary allowlist with no floor exception. It is not coupled to an Observer, so no Observer can block the call.
ROUND TOPIC (F4). One topic per principal per round, opened by the mechanism's record and sealed on emit: the unit of erasure. Kafka is neither the ordering authority nor the system of record.
ARCHIVE † (F4). The system of record for control-plane facts.
PAYLOAD STORE † (F4). Cognitive payloads, kept apart from the facts and built for deletion.
ERASURE † (F5). A privileged, modeled, consensus-ordered event, and the floor's one exception.
FORENSIC FLOOR (F5). Six classes survive erasure: F1 admit decisions, F2 stop attribution, F3 promotion votes, F4 anchor issuances, F5 activations, F6 erasure events.
AUDIT AUTHORITY (F5). Reads the record: replay of boundary events, for the declared horizon.
CELL OBSERVER (E4). One per cell, deny-only. It reads the cell's round topics, and sends heartbeats, findings and Vote(deny).
HEARTBEAT (D4). Liveness is progress, not presence: heard within T_obs, and seq − mark < K. Run couples every effect to it; Build couples the gate.
CORRELATOR † (E5). Named folds over facts: five correlations a second reader can recompute. Never coupled.
PINNED CONTENT (G6). The corpus root in Build and the Run root: content-addressed, reached by Read and Consult.
LISTENER (F6). A stage, not a seat. It delivers the task, admitted reads and results, and makes no choice.
LABELS (E6). Every item of Run's ingress carries a label: a function of its source, and no judgment about content.
CLEAR OR HANDLE (D6). An item arrives clear, and joins clearSet, or as a handle: a name and no bytes. Forbids R5 to R7 tighten with what was read.
TOOL LIST (C6). A Thinker learns its tools from the mechanism. The list is the round's opening record.

g.text: The archetype, as the records draw it.
The only way from Build to Run
